messages:
Casey (support): hey team — customer reported embeddings producing a 400 with 'dimension mismatch' and billing spiked. forwarding convo. Sam (prod) pasted logs below.
Sam (prod): their repro: single API hit resulted in 10x billed vectors. says they only sent one doc. link: https://customer-logs/redwood/abc123
Casey (support): can you paste the exact payload they sent? often it's shape/encoding related (single vs list) or accidental extra nesting from their client lib.
Sam (prod): here is the body from their client (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED

{"model": "text-embedding-ada-002", "input": [ [ [0.1, 0.2, ... 0.3] ] ] }
```
Sam (prod): note the triple nesting — they wrapped the vector twice by mistake. they thought the client would unwrap.
Casey (support): oh yea that explains dimension mismatch and billing. server interprets first level as list-of-requests and second level as list-of-vectors -> each inner array counted as a vector. billing increments by number of vectors.
Devin (infra): confirmed from logs: request_id=ix-7a9  payload_vectors=10  inferred_vector_len=1536 expected_len=1536  error emitted: "vector length mismatch". but the billing pipeline already tallied 10 vectors before validation returned 400.
Julia (billing): so they were charged for 10 vectors despite the call failing? need chargeback/credit. tag me with customer id and invoice.
Casey (support): noted. @Julia I'll create a support ticket and request urgent credit. customer id: cust-7782. invoice: inv-2026-03-12-88.
Sam (prod): customer says they send arrays from Python: `np.array(...).tolist()` then `json.dumps(payload)`. guess double-wrapping happened in framework.
Devin (infra): root cause summary: client sent nested list-of-list-of-list. runtime treated outer list as batch, middle lists as vectors, inner numbers as components. validation fails because some vectors have wrong length or too nested. billing counts before deep schema validation.
Casey (support): next steps: 1) produce a short repro to reproduce locally 2) provide workaround and corrected payload to customer 3) billing credit 4) infra: avoid charging for invalid requests in future (defer billing until validation).
Sam (prod): repro I used locally:
```
# bad
payload = {"model":"text-embedding-ada-002","input": [ [[0.1,0.2,...]], [[0.3,0.4,...]] ] }
# server sees 2 vectors (outer list len 2) where inner arrays are vectors but nested arrays cause length errors

# good
payload = {"model":"text-embedding-ada-002","input": [[0.1,0.2,...],[0.3,0.4,...]]}
```
Sam (prod): also saw people send a single vector without outer list: `"input": [0.1,0.2,...]` — that works with some wrappers but our runtime expects a list of vectors (outer list).
Casey (support): can we craft an enhanced error message? Right now the 400 is generic: "dimension mismatch". Suggest: "Invalid embedding input shape: expected list of vectors, e.g. [[...],[...]] but got nested arrays. If you intended a single vector, wrap it in an outer list."
Devin (infra): good idea. quick patch: detect if any element of input is not a number but a list — if depth>2 return explicit guidance and do not increment billing counters. I can have a small patch to validation pipeline today.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: patch/emb-validate-raise-msg -> infra-staging at 1798504500
Devin (infra): deploying to staging now. also adding telemetry metric emb.invalid_shape_count and emb.charged_on_invalid_flag.
Casey (support): meanwhile message to customer with clear repro and fix. Sam can you write a short snippet they can paste (JS + Python)?
Sam (prod): Sure. JS fix snippet: 
```
// bad
const payload = { model: 'text-embedding-ada-002', input: [ [ [0.1,0.2,...] ] ] }

// good (single vector)
const payload = { model: 'text-embedding-ada-002', input: [[0.1,0.2,...]] }
```
Python snippet: 
```
# bad
payload = {"model":"text-embedding-ada-002", "input": numpy_array.tolist() }
# good - ensure outer list
payload = {"model":"text-embedding-ada-002", "input": [ numpy_array.tolist() ] }
```
Casey (support): FYI also include a small explanation about billing: "You may have been billed for multiple vectors because the server interpreted your nested arrays as multiple vectors. We've issued a refund while infra works on validation."
Julia (billing): I created a credit for invoice inv-2026-03-12-88: credit_id=cr-904f. note: we should also add a backend guard to prevent tallying until validation complete. putting that on infra + billing follow-up.
Devin (infra): quick note from staging run: new validator rejects depth>2 with 422 and message: "Invalid input nesting: expected list of vectors [[...]], found deeper nesting. Wrap single vectors in an outer array. No billing applied for rejected requests."
Casey (support): perfect. pushing to prod after run-through. ETA prod deploy in 2h.
deploy-bot: deploy successful: patch/emb-validate-raise-msg -> infra-prod at 1798504700 :tada:
Devin (infra): prod live. I also added a small log sample to help support triage automatically: if emb.invalid_shape_count > 0 then auto-attach sanitized payload to support ticket.
Casey (support): I sent the customer the corrected snippets and the credit info. waiting for confirmation they can resume.
Sam (prod): customer confirmed their integration now works with the outer-list fix. :thumbsup: thanks team.
Casey (support): follow-up items for docs: add explicit 'input' shape examples (single vector, batch of vectors, nested arrays pitfalls) and a note on billing semantics. I'll file a docs ticket.
Julia (billing): closing billing loop once customer acknowledges credit applied.
Devin (infra): long term: consider accepting both single-vector and outer-list forms and normalize server-side, but that's a larger change. for now explicit error + no-bill on validation error is good.
Casey (support): excellent. closing thread when customer confirms. thanks everyone.
